newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokuma Shoten to take 10 pct DirecTV Japan stake.
newsitem.headline: Tokuma Shoten to take 10 pct DirecTV Japan stake.

text.p: Tokuma Shoten Publishing Co Ltd will take a 10 percent equity interest in satellite broadcaster DirecTV Japan, DirecTV Japan chairman Gareth Chang told a news conference on Thursday.

After the news conference, Hughes Electronics Corp Chairman Micheal Armstrong told reporters that DirecTV is in "serious discussions" with a Japanese broadcaster regarding the broadcaster taking a stake in DirecTV Japan Co Ltd.

He declined to name the broadcaster, although when asked during the news conference if DirecTV was in talks with Nippon Television Network Corp on an equity stake in DirecTV Japan, Armstrong said, "We would be honoured if they would consider participation."
Hughes, a subsidiary of General Motors Corp, is the lead shareholder in U.S. satellite broadcaster DirecTV, which owns 35 percent of DirecTV Japan.
Armstrong said DirecTV Japan was likely to begin broadcasting in November or December this year and to offer 72 to 96 channels.
He declined to give a target for DirecTV subscribers in Japan, although he said half of Japan's 40 million households are potential subscribers.
He added that the uplink of the company's Ibaraki broadcasting centre was proceeding according to schedule.

Armstrong, who is in charge of worldwide strategy for DirecTV, was in Tokyo to meet DirecTV's partners in Japan, which include Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Corp and four other Japanese companies, and with officials of Japan's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.
Last year Tokuma Shoten concluded a deal with Walt Disney Studios under which Disney will distribute animated movies made for Tokuma by Hayao Miyazaki, one of Asia's top animators.
